questions.question: Which of the following best defines non-experimental research?

answers.text: Research that lacks the manipulation of an independent variable
Research that always uses qualitative data
Research that is conducted only in laboratory settings
Research that randomly assigns participants to conditions

questions.question: According to the chapter, which statement about the relationship between experimental and non-experimental research is most accurate?

answers.text: Non-experimental research is less important than experimental research
Experimental research can provide strong evidence of causation, while non-experimental research generally cannot
Non-experimental research always has higher external validity than experimental research
Experimental research is appropriate only when ethical concerns prevent manipulation

questions.question: When would non-experimental research be most appropriate?

answers.text: When the research question pertains to a causal relationship and random assignment is possible
When the independent variable cannot be manipulated for practical or ethical reasons
When the goal is exclusively to explain behavior
When studying simple relationships between two quantitative variables

questions.question: In correlational research, what does a Pearson's r value of -0.85 indicate?

answers.text: A weak negative relationship
A strong positive relationship
A strong negative relationship
No relationship between the variables

questions.question: What is the 'directionality problem' in correlational research?

answers.text: The difficulty in determining whether variables have a positive or negative correlation
The inability to determine whether X causes Y or Y causes X
The challenge of measuring variables in the correct order
The problem of choosing the right statistical test

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of the 'third-variable problem'?

answers.text: Exercise causes happiness through improved physical health
Physical health causes both exercise and happiness
Happiness causes people to exercise more frequently
Exercise and happiness are measured using three different scales

questions.question: According to the chapter, what is a major limitation of Pearson's r?

answers.text: It cannot measure relationships between categorical variables
It is only a good measure for linear relationships
It can only detect positive correlations
It requires a minimum sample size of 1,000 participants

questions.question: What is 'restriction of range' in correlational research?

answers.text: When the correlation coefficient is limited to values between 0 and 1
When one or both variables have a limited range in the sample relative to the population
When researchers only collect data from a narrow geographic area
When participants are restricted from discussing their responses

questions.question: In cross-sectional studies, what is the primary concern when comparing different age groups?

answers.text: Random assignment cannot be used
Differences may reflect cohort effects rather than true age effects
The studies take too long to complete
Participants may drop out over time

questions.question: What distinguishes participant observation from naturalistic observation?

answers.text: Participant observation always takes place in laboratory settings
In participant observation, researchers become active members of the group being studied
Naturalistic observation requires informed consent while participant observation does not
Participant observation can only be conducted with disguised identities

questions.question: According to the chapter, what is a key advantage of qualitative research?

answers.text: It provides precise statistical answers to specific research questions
It can generate new and interesting research questions and provide rich descriptions of behavior
It eliminates the need for reliability and validity considerations
It always has higher internal validity than quantitative research

questions.question: What is 'grounded theory' in qualitative research?

answers.text: A method where researchers start with a theory and test specific hypotheses
An approach where researchers develop a theory that is 'grounded in' the data they collect
A technique for conducting observations in natural ground-level settings
A statistical method for analyzing qualitative data

questions.question: What does 'reactivity' refer to in observational research?

answers.text: When participants react emotionally to the research topic
When a measure changes participants' behavior
When researchers react to unexpected findings
When chemical reactions occur during physiological measurements

questions.question: Which type of study involves following one group of people over time as they age?

answers.text: Cross-sectional study
Longitudinal study
Cross-sequential study
Correlational study

questions.question: What is factor analysis primarily used for?

answers.text: Testing whether one variable causes another
Organizing many variables into smaller clusters based on correlation patterns
Calculating the reliability of a single measurement
Determining sample size for experimental studies

questions.question: According to the chapter, what is a key limitation of case studies?

answers.text: They provide too little detail about individual participants
They suffer from problems with both internal and external validity
They can only be conducted in laboratory settings
They always require quantitative data analysis

questions.question: What is 'partial correlation' used for in complex correlational research?

answers.text: Measuring only part of a relationship between two variables
Examining the relationship between two variables while statistically controlling for third variables
Calculating correlations with incomplete data sets
Determining which portion of variance is due to measurement error

questions.question: In structured observation, what is 'coding'?

answers.text: Encrypting participant data to ensure confidentiality
Categorizing participants' behaviors according to clearly defined target behaviors
Assigning numerical codes to replace participant names
Programming computer software to collect data

questions.question: According to the chapter, when can correlation establish causation?

answers.text: When the correlation coefficient exceeds +0.80 or -0.80
When combined with longitudinal research designs
Correlation cannot unambiguously establish causation
When third variables have been measured and controlled statistically

questions.question: What is 'triangulation' in the context of combining quantitative and qualitative research?

answers.text: Using three different statistical tests to analyze the same data
Using both methods simultaneously to study the same questions and comparing results
Dividing participants into three equal groups for comparison
Collecting data from three different geographic locations
